current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let
$(B,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be an equicharacteristic Noetherian local domain, and
let $(B_n,\mathfrak m_n)$, $n\ge0$, be the local rings at a successive
infinite chain of point blowups, $B_0=B$, all with residue field $\kappa$: for
every $n$ the ring $B_{n+1}$ is the local ring at a point of the blowup
$\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathfrak m_n}(B_n)$ of the closed point, the structural
maps $B_n\to B_{n+1}$ are local, and $B_{n+1}/\mathfrak m_{n+1}=\kappa$, compatibly with the specified residue-field maps.
Suppose that one element $t\in\mathfrak m$ generates the pullback of every
centre ideal on the next local ring:

$$\mathfrak m_nB_{n+1}=tB_{n+1}\qquad(n\ge0).$$

Then there is a nonsingular formal arc $B\to V$, extended from a surjection
$\widehat B\to V$, whose point-blowup centres are the given ones. Here $V$ is a
complete discrete valuation ring with residue field $\kappa$ and uniformizer
the image of $t$; no chosen coefficient-field identification is needed.

current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition: Assume AC and DC. Let $A$ be a nonregular rational normal local surface domain in the permitted canonical-module setting, with $\omega_A\cong A$. Then its point blowup is normal with trivial canonical module. Its exceptional conormal $L$ has degree two and $\dim_\kappa\mathfrak m^n/\mathfrak m^{n+1}=2n+1$. For a minimal generating triple of $\mathfrak m$, the associated graded ring is $\kappa[T_1,T_2,T_3]/(q)$ for one nonzero quadratic $q$, so the exceptional fibre is its plane conic.

current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition: Assume AC and DC. For a nonregular rational normal local surface domain in the permitted regular-base dualizing setting, let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ be its ordinary point blowup, $E$ its exceptional divisor and $I=O_X(1)$. Then $H^1(X,\omega_X\otimes I^n)=0$ for $n\ge0$ and the canonical evaluation $f^*\omega_A\to\omega_X$ is surjective. The assertion localizes to closed rational singular points on a projective normal modification of the same regular base.

If a permitted normal local surface domain $A$ is rational and $A\subset B$ is a normal two-dimensional local domain with the same fraction field, essentially of finite type over $A$, then $B$ is rational. If modification H1 over $A$ is uniformly bounded, some finite normalized point-blowup sequence over $A$ has rational local rings at every closed point of its terminal surface.

current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition: Assume AC. Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring, $\widehat A$ its maximal-adic completion, and $X$ a scheme locally of finite type over $A$. Put $Y=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$. The closed fibres of $X$ and $Y$ are canonically isomorphic. If $y\in Y$ lies on this fibre and $x$ is its corresponding point, then the local homomorphism $\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ induces an isomorphism of maximal-adic completions.

current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition: Assume AC and DC. For a rational Gorenstein normal local surface singularity with square tangent conic, choose $\mathfrak m=(x_1,x_2,z)$ and a relation $z^2=\sum a_{ijk}x_ix_jx_k$. There is a nonzero homogeneous cubic $H\in\kappa[X_1,X_2]$ whose zero scheme on the reduced exceptional line contains all singular successors. Simple closed zeros have nonsquare successor conic and therefore finite resolution. There is at most one possible square-conic successor, and it is $\kappa$-rational. This is a branching statement, not termination of the continuing square branch.

current_supplier_interfaces.statement_or_definition: Assume AC and DC. A normal two-dimensional Noetherian local domain $A$ essentially of finite type over a field or complete equicharacteristic local base defines a rational singularity if $H^1(Y,\mathcal O_Y)=0$ for every normal integral proper modification $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. Bounded modification H1 means these modules have uniformly bounded $A$-length. In both definitions it suffices to test projective modifications, or terminal schemes of finite normalized point-blowup sequences.

characteristic_independent_arc_audit: The standard blowup charts embed the chain in the original fraction field. Locality gives a local directed union U with residue field kappa.
The fixed-coordinate hypothesis gives n=tU. Nonzero t and cancellation, not a coefficient field, give the successive quotient identifications.
The t-adic inverse limit V has ker(pi_N)=t^NV and t is a nonzerodivisor. Compatible division proves both facts before asserting V is a domain.
Completeness inverts 1+tV; separatedness gives finite orders; minimal ideal order proves V is a Noetherian one-dimensional regular local domain, hence a complete DVR.
The completion surjection uses arbitrary residue lifts c_i in A and their convergent sum sum(c_it^i). This works in mixed characteristic and in equicharacteristic. AC/DC supply the choices.
Each B_n maps locally to V and m_nV=tV. The blowup universal property identifies the centres with the original chain.
The termination supplier itself assumes no characteristic condition. Applied to the given normal completion, it uses the regular height-one kernel and generator/exponent descent.
Flat blowup base change and equality of closed-fibre completed local rings transfer finite terminal regularity back to the original chain.

edits.old: 5.1 If an infinite chain of singular point blowups existed, its centres would be $\kappa$-rational with residue field $\kappa$ and the fixed element $x_1$ would generate the pullback of every centre ideal, so the fixed-coordinate helper would construct a nonsingular formal arc, namely a surjection from the completion of $A$ onto a complete discrete valuation ring with uniformizer the image of $x_1$ whose point-blowup centres are the given ones; $\kappa$-rationality and rationality of the local rings propagate along the chain, and normal completion persists by the regular-fibre normality result. [F5, F10, F11, step 4.1]
edits.new:
5.1 Suppose the continuing singular chain is infinite, and write its local rings as $(B_n,\mathfrak m_n)$ with $B_0=A$. The preceding chart argument gives compatible residue fields $\kappa$ and $\mathfrak m_nB_{n+1}=x_1B_{n+1}$. The standard charts embed all $B_n$ in $\operatorname{Frac}A$, so $U=\bigcup_nB_n$ is a local domain with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\bigcup_n\mathfrak m_n=x_1U$ and residue field $\kappa$: every element outside that union is already a unit in some $B_n$. The element $x_1$ is a nonzero nonunit. [F5, step 4.1, algebra]

5.2 Put $V=\varprojlim_{N\ge1}U/x_1^NU$. Its projections $\pi_N$ are surjective, since a representative in $U$ gives a compatible system. Cancellation in the domain $U$ identifies $U/x_1^jU$ with $x_1^NU/x_1^{N+j}U$. Thus for $v\in\ker\pi_N$, uniquely dividing its component at $N+j$ by $x_1^N$ gives compatible components $w_j$ and $v=x_1^Nw$; hence $\ker\pi_N=x_1^NV$. Also multiplication by $x_1^N$ on $V$ is injective: if $x_1^Nw=0$, its component at $N+j$ forces $w_j=0$ for every $j$. Therefore $V/x_1^NV\cong U/x_1^NU$, $V$ is $x_1$-adically complete, and $\bigcap_Nx_1^NV=0$. [step 5.1, construct, algebra]

5.3 Since $V/x_1V=\kappa$, an element outside $x_1V$ is a unit: lift its nonzero residue by a unit $u\in U$, write it as $u(1+e)$ with $e\in x_1V$, and invert $1+e$ by its convergent geometric series. Every nonzero $v\in V$ consequently has the form $x_1^Nu$ for a unit $u$, with finite $N$ by separatedness. Injectivity of multiplication by powers of $x_1$ shows that products of nonzero elements are nonzero. Every nonzero ideal has an element of least order $N$ and is then $(x_1^N)$; thus $V$ is Noetherian, its only primes are $0$ and $x_1V$, and its maximal ideal is principal. Hence $V$ is a complete DVR with uniformizer $x_1$ and residue field $\kappa$. [F14, step 5.2, algebra]

5.4 The local maps $B_n\to V$ identify residue fields and satisfy $\mathfrak m_nV=x_1V$. Completeness extends $A\to V$ to $\widehat A\to V$. This extension is surjective: for $v\in V$ recursively choose $c_i\in A$ with the residue of $r_i$, starting with $r_0=v$, and put $r_{i+1}=(r_i-c_i)/x_1$. Then $s_N=\sum_{i<N}c_ix_1^i$ is maximal-adically Cauchy in $A$ and $v-s_N=x_1^Nr_N$. Its limit in $\widehat A$ maps to $v$ by separatedness. The residue choices use AC and DC; no coefficient field or characteristic assumption enters. [F1, F2, F12, step 5.2, step 5.3, choose, algebra]

5.5 The image of $x_1\in\mathfrak m$ is a uniformizer, so $A\to V$ is a nonsingular formal arc. At every $B_n$ its centre ideal pulls back to the effective Cartier divisor $(x_1)$ on $\operatorname{Spec}V$. The blowup universal property gives the unique next lift; the local map $B_{n+1}\to V$ supplies that lift and places its closed point at the prescribed centre. Thus this arc has exactly the given chain of centres. [F13, F5, step 5.1, step 5.3, step 5.4]
